report:
Left fallopian tube, salpingectomy

Received in formalin is a distended segment of tubal tissue measuring 4 x 2 x 2 cm. A segment of left fallopian tube is identified measuring 5 cm long, and its lumen is distended, up to 2 cm across. The cut surface of the fallopian tube tissue shows extensive blood clot within the tubal lumen, as well as spongy material. There is a rupture site measuring 1.5 cm on the serosal surface. The fimbrial end is identified. A separate blood clot measuring 3 x 2 x 1 cm is also received. No foetal parts are grossly identified. 4 representative blocks.

(1) Uninvolved fallopian tube.
(2)&(3) Haemorrhagic tubal tissue with distension.
(4) Separate blood clot.

The sections show chorionic villi and haemorrhage within the lumen of the fallopian tube. There is disruption of the tubal wall, in keeping with rupture. The tubal epithelium is unremarkable. There is no evidence of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia or other malignancies.

Left FALLOPIAN TUBE, salpingectomy - ECTOPIC TUBAL PREGNANCY with RUPTURE
